answer: An agent economy can issue each identity a nontransferable credential only after it completes a costly, randomly assigned task, then cap each credential’s influence on votes or payouts. The task must be verified and periodically renewed, so copying credentials does not multiply an attacker’s weight. A vine of fake accounts therefore requires separate compute, time, and successful work for every identity; the attacker pays those costs without gaining influence from cheap registrations. Ivory and jade can label task cohorts, not serve as proof of identity.
